events.text: John Pesutto becomes Liberal leader and leader of the opposition
Jacinta Allan becomes Labor leader and premier
Brad Battin becomes Liberal leader and leader of the opposition
Jess Wilson is elected Liberal leader and leader of the Opposition
Jacinta Allan resigns as leader of the Labor Party and premier; Ben Carroll is elected leader and premier
Warren Pickering becomes state leader of One Nation

winnability.source: Roy Morgan, Finding No. 10346, "Victorian Election is too close to call today", 9 October 2026 (Appendix 1)
winnability.description: Roy Morgan's One Nation Winnability Score ranks all 88 districts (1 = most winnable) by combining current voting intention with how closely each electorate's voter profile matches One Nation's core support base. Roy Morgan projects 11 One Nation seats from the same data but has not published which; the ranking is the nearest public guide.

issues.source: Herald Sun / Freshwater Strategy monthly Victorian poll, published data tables (online panel, ~1,000 Victorian voters a wave, weighted to age, sex, education, 2022 state and 2025 federal vote, location)

internal.source: Guardian Australia, 1 Nov 2026: Is One Nation losing steam in Victoria?
internal.notes: Effective sample 1,488, MoE 3%. Greens say the upper-house question gave consistent figures; they read it as holding Richmond, Melbourne and Brunswick, winning Prahran and Northcote, and in contention in Pascoe Vale and Footscray.

seat_polls.title: Bass, Hastings, Morwell and Pakenham
seat_polls.primary_note: Combined primary vote for Hastings, Morwell and Pakenham
seat_polls.notes: 283 electors across four seats, so roughly 70 per seat: indicative only. 'Never vote for': ALP 44%, One Nation 41%, Greens 37%, Coalition 12%; 40% of Coalition voters would never vote One Nation, 10% of One Nation voters would never vote Coalition.
